text:
Ana: quick dump from the profiler — saw a shift in prefill vs decode after the kernel switch, thought i'd share raw numbers
Josh: thanks, drop it here pls
Ana: past-hour aggregate (mixed-cust load):
```
prefill_total_tokens: 38%\nprefill_p50: 22ms, p95: 90ms\ndecode_total_tokens: 62%\ndecode_p50: 28ms, p95: 260ms\nend-to-end p95 per-request: 320ms (long tails on decode-heavy short prompts)
```
Maria: interesting — decode p95 jumped after we enabled the AVX fallback kernel?
Ana: yeah timeline matches the kernel rollout at 20:12 UTC. AVX path seems faster for long seq but fallback path is much worse for 1-4 token decode bursts
Ryan: can you attach the perf heatmap? want to see microbatch sizes vs kernel selection
Ana: pasted below, note x-axis microbatch size, y-axis latency percentile. green = preferred kernel, orange = fallback
```
mbatch 1..8: kernel A preferred for prefill
mbatch 9..32: kernel B preferred for decode on longer seqs
mbatch 1..4 decode: fallback kernel chosen ~18% of runs
```
Sophie: is fallback selection deterministic by sequence length or by runtime probe?
Josh: it's the runtime probe + kernel safety margin. if kernel A reports instability we pick B. looks like probe false-positive for short decode bursts
Maria: could be KV cache contention too — decode short bursts touch KV more often (evictions) and trigger slower paths
Ana: i ran a synthetic: pinned KV warm vs cold, results show decode p95 drops ~70ms when KV is warm for the same microbatch sizes
Ryan: so two orthogonal levers: microbatch sizing and KV prefetching/warming. which gives better SLO win per-cost?
Sophie: microbatch bump: fewer kernel switches, higher throughput but p50 improves and p99 might worsen depending on burstiness
Josh: for our SLO (p95 < 250ms) we need to focus decode tail first — that's the blocker for short prompt interactive flows
Ana: proposal: for interactive routes, cap microbatch at 6 and prefer kernel A for decode even if probe is marginal. add conservative KV prefetch for first decode token. instrumentation: trace kernel decision + kv-hit per request
Maria: sounds reasonable. we should also add a metric for "kernel-fallback-rate" per route and alarm if >5% sustained
perf-bot: deploy plan created: canary 5% traffic -> 20% -> 100% with automatic rollback on p95 increase >10% over baseline
Ryan: also want an offline sim: replay 12h prod traces with proposed cap=6 and prefetch=on to measure token-cost delta
Ana: i've got a replay script, use flag --kv-prefetch and --mbatch-cap. command:
```
./replay --trace=prod-2026-03-15.gz --mbatch-cap=6 --kv-prefetch=1 --output=results.json
```
Sophie: small note: prefetching increases GPU memory throughput and may reduce throughput on Dedicated nodes during peak. need quota knob per-node
Josh: agree, include a per-node prefetch budget. also include a cheap heuristic: only prefetch when expected decode length > 1 token (avoid waste for 0-1 token responses)
Maria: will add regression test to perf-suite: assert decode p95 <= 250ms for the interactive route with 95% of traces replayed
Ana: timeline: I'll run the offline replay overnight, open a canary PR for runtime probe tweak + prefetch flag tomorrow morning. want to ship next week if numbers look good
Ryan: nice. if replay shows throughput regressions >8% we pivot to hybrid: prefetch only on kernel-stable nodes
Josh: thanks Ana — appreciate the triage. ping me when replay done, i'll help interpret results
Ana: will do. tagging @Sophie for infra knobs and @Maria for perf-suite tests :eyes:
